newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Colt frontrunner to buy Belgian arms maker.
newsitem.headline: Colt frontrunner to buy Belgian arms maker.

text.p: U.S. gunmaker Colt emerged Friday as the frontrunner to acquire Belgian arms maker Herstal SA from French state-controlled defence group GIAT.
Belgium's Walloon Regional Government, which owns an 8 percent stake in Herstal, said it discussed a sale with representatives of the U.S. firm on Friday and planned further talks next week.
"At the moment they are the only candidate buyers," a source close to Herstal told Reuters.
Belgian newspapers have said Italy's Beretta Holding, in which Herstal has a minority interest, was also a potential buyer.
A spokesman for the Walloon government was not immediately available to comment.
The acquisition would combine some of the world's best-known gun makerrs. Herstal owns the Browning and Winchester names, making weapons for civilian use.
Its FN unit supplies military hardware, including Colt's M16-A2 rifles and machine guns for the U.S. army produced at a subsidiary in North Carolina.
In 1990 GIAT paid about 800 million Belgian francs (then $26 million) for a majority stake in money-losing Herstal bought from holding company Societe Generale de Belgique.
GIAT hoped to turn the company round, but the downturn in the worldwide defence industry following the end of the Cold War left both firms struggling.
Herstal last made a small profit in 1994. It lost around 380 million francs ($10.5 million) in 1995, while 1996's figures have not been published.
Belgian media have reported Herstal's 1996 sales were down to 14 billion francs ($387 million) from 17.5 billion ($485 million) in 1995.
Paris has authorised GIAT to suspend publishing its accounts for last year until the future of Herstal has become clearer.

Announcing a drastic restructuring plan at the end of 1996, Herstal hoped to return to an operating profit only from 1998. It estimated it would need investments of five billion francs ($138 million) over the four years to 2000, which would only partly be covered by a plan to sell its minority interest in Beretta.
